defects: The whole 30 s is one locked-off shot with no camera move, scale change or reframing; 20 of 29 seconds read almost the same as the second before.
The main motion is a year counter ticking over and rings being added one at a time at an even rate. The pairs show the year advancing by one with no easing, overshoot or settle.
The '1979–88 average' legend fades in through a long, muddy half-opacity state (frame 5) and is never shown cleanly before it changes.
The orange 2012 minimum ring and the dot on the line chart just appear. Nothing about the timing marks them as the record low.
The left caption about each ring and the right column of text and chart are two separate reading paths with no motion connecting them.
The ice disc is a flat vector fill with a radial gradient and a soft glow. At 100% it has no surface detail and no light beyond the gradient.
The ending reuses the same layout as frame 5 and adds only a legend line and '−35%'. The figure appears without any build.

In the soundtrack, roughly 1 s chord blocks repeat on a fixed grid with pluck-like partials. The only dynamic change is added density from about 13 s and a decay tail from about 26 s. It sounds like a looped bed, not sound design scored to the picture.
The audio blocks follow a fixed grid. The picture has no cuts or impacts, so nothing visible can land on the transients.
gaps: Choreography and timing: the year sweep needs a speed curve (fast through stable years, slowing into the decline years and the 2012 record) and a real held climax. The rings need overlap and follow-through as each one settles, and the closing comparison needs a staged camera push or reframe. Without these it plays as a linear data tick inside one static frame.

Sound: the music should be a scored bed with sound design tied to the data, for example a tick or crackle per year, a weighted hit on the record low and on '−35%', and real dynamic contrast. Right now it is a repeating, loudness-normalised loop.

Finish and visual payoff: the ice needs texture and light falloff, and the type needs a hierarchy that carries meaning, for example year size or weight following extent. The ending should rhyme with the opening frame rather than just adding a legend to the frame before it.
